artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part RE DeJong's complaint against Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church (Rocky Mountain Presbytery), upholding Session's creation of a Judicial Commission and its recommendation to remove term limit restrictions for ruling elders, but annulling Session's creation of a Governance Commission because two provisions of the governing document unconstitutionally allowed the commission to function like the Session itself, exceeding the limits placed on commissions by BCO 15-1.

artifacts.title: Speck v. Missouri Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part TE Ryan Speck's complaint against Missouri Presbytery's December 2019 adoption of six theological judgments regarding the 2018 Revoice Conference hosted by Memorial Presbyterian Church, ruling that MOP applied an incorrect constitutional standard (BCO 34-5 'vitals of religion') rather than the proper BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f) criteria, and failed to take adequate action with respect to erroneous teachings identified by its own committees regarding terminology (TJ 2), the 'gay beneath the gay' (TJ 3), and spiritual friendships (TJ 5); the matter was remanded to MOP with instructions for a new hearing. Dissenting opinions were filed by RE John D. Pickering and TE David F. Coffin, Jr., who argued that the SJC improperly raised an issue not presented by either party in violation of BCO 39-3.1.

artifacts.title: Payne v. Western Carolina Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Martin Payne and related complainants challenged Western Carolina Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of accusations concerning TE Craig Bulkeley and its conclusion that no strong presumption of guilt existed. The SJC denied the specifications, holding that BCO 31-2 gives the investigating court great discretion over procedure and timing and that the record did not show clear error; related complainants lacked standing.

artifacts.title: Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaints of TE Eliot Lee against Korean Eastern Presbytery (cases 2007-09 and 2007-10). KEP erred when it empowered the Pulpit Commission to act on behalf of the church session without proper consent, and erred when it filed a civil action against TE Lee to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters. The decision affirms the non-hierarchical, voluntary nature of the PCA and its limited jurisdiction in civil matters.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained an appeal by E. L. Fitzsimmons against Evangel Presbytery's handling of his appeal from excommunication. The court found that Presbytery erred by failing to notify the appellant of the time, date, and place for hearing the appeal and by rescinding its earlier finding that the appeal was in order, thus failing to adjudicate the appeal properly. The case was remanded to Evangel Presbytery for proper adjudication on the merits.

artifacts.title: Nickoley v. Rocky Mountain
artifacts.synopsis: Rocky Mountain Presbytery erred in immediately deposing Rev. Bruce Nickoley for contumacy without giving him reasonable opportunity to defend himself under the due process provisions of the Book of Church Order. The case was remanded to the presbytery with recommendations to either institute a formal prosecution with due process or revoke the deposition and reinstate Nickoley.
